What the second hosted session on v0.1.71 showed, and the two things it changes.

## Server

### Fixed
- A returning player now gets their own save from the game's first load. The client joins with a blank platform identity and asks for a blank record; the host answered that request, then re-issued the load with the player's synthetic id a tick later. The client kept the blank answer: a fresh character with starting items, while the server-side pawn was holding the real inventory, which is also why used items stuck in the quickbar. The blank key is now rewritten in place before the game runs the load, so the first answer is the right one. The re-issued load stays as the fallback and the log line `BeginLoadData key rewritten ... landed=true` says which path a join took.
- The host no longer enumerates the game's save-system class after the world is hosted. The game's own player-triggered saves create and destroy a transient save object, and touching that class while one was pending destruction crashed the host inside the mod loader a second after the save-folder sweep, twice, both times with a player online. Only the stable game-instance and save-manager singletons are enforced at runtime; the class walk is pre-host only.

### Changed
- The machine-name alias file only records a machine-derived name pointing at a real character name, never the reverse.
